leftEvidence.title: God delights in the servant and puts the Spirit on him

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: God presents a chosen servant, delights in him, and puts his Spirit on him for justice among the nations.
points.right: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized; John resists, Jesus answers, and the baptism proceeds.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The servant acts without public display, preserves what is bruised, and becomes covenant and light.
points.right: Opened heavens, descending Spirit, and a heavenly voice identify the beloved Son in whom God delights.

payload.posture: Divine delight and Spirit language make Isaiah 42 a material source for hearing Matthew’s voice.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus comes to John and speaks of fulfilling righteousness

payload.tension: The Gospel wording is not a single-source verbatim quotation.
payload.title: The delighted servant and beloved Son
